LMNL.text: Of that forbidden tree whose mortal taste
That shepherd who first taught the chosen seed
In the beginning how the heavens and earth
Fast by the oracle of God
Invoke thy aid to my adventurous song
That with no middle flight intends to soar
Things unattempted yet in prose or rhyme
Before all temples th' upright heart and pure
Dove-like sat'st brooding on the vast Abyss
what is low raise and support
to the height of this great argument
And justify the ways of God to men
for Heaven hides nothing from thy view
Nor the deep tract of Hell
Who first seduced them to that foul revolt
Stirred up with envy and revenge
Had cast him out from Heaven
To set himself in glory above his peers
He trusted to have equalled the Most High
Against the throne and monarchy of God
Raised impious war in Heaven and battle proud
Hurled headlong flaming from th' ethereal sky
In adamantine chains and penal fire
Who durst defy th' Omnipotent to arms
Nine times the space that measures day and night
Both of lost happiness and lasting pain
round he throws his baleful eyes
That witnessed huge affliction and dismay
Mixed with obdurate pride and steadfast hate
The dismal situation waste and wild
Served only to discover sights of woe
Such place Eternal Justice has prepared
As far removed from God and light of Heaven
As from the centre thrice to th' utmost pole
Oh how unlike the place from whence they fell
There the companions of his fall
With floods and whirlwinds of tempestuous fire
And thence in Heaven called Satan

The pilot of some small night-foundered skiff
With fixed anchor in his scaly rind
Moors by his side under the lee
So stretched out huge in length the Arch-fiend lay
And high permission of all-ruling Heaven
Left him at large to his own dark designs
That with reiterated crimes he might
How all his malice served but to bring forth
Forthwith upright he rears from off the pool
Driven backward slope their pointing spires
leave i' th' midst a horrid vale
Then with expanded wings he steers his flight
if it were land that ever burned
as the lake with liquid fire
And such appeared in hue as when the force
Of subterranean wind transports a hill
And leave a singed bottom all involved
Both glorying to have scaped the Stygian flood
and by their own recovered strength
Not by the sufferance of supernal Power

LMNL.text: as when men wont to watch
sleeping found by whom they dread
Rouse and bestir themselves ere well awake
Nor did they not perceive the evil plight
or the fierce pains not feel
Yet to their General's voice they soon obeyed
That o'er the realm of impious Pharaoh hung
and darkened all the land of Nile
So numberless were those bad Angels seen
Hovering on wing under the cope of Hell
Of their great Sultan waving to direct
in even balance down they light
A multitude like which the populous North
Poured never from her frozen loins to pass
Came like a deluge on the South
Beneath Gibraltar to the Libyan sands
from every squadron and each band
The heads and leaders thither haste where stood
And Powers that erst in Heaven sat on thrones
Though on their names in Heavenly records now
By their rebellion from the Books of Life
Nor had they yet among the sons of Eve
Through God's high sufferance for the trial of man
By falsities and lies the greatest part
Of mankind they corrupted to forsake
Glory of him that made them to transform
Oft to the image of a brute
With gay religions full of pomp and gold
And devils to adore for deities
Then were they known to men by various names
And various idols through the heathen world
Roused from the slumber on that fiery couch
Came singly where he stood on the bare strand
While the promiscuous crowd stood yet aloof
Roaming to seek their prey on Earth
Within his sanctuary itself their shrines
His holy rites and solemn feasts profaned
And with their darkness durst affront his light
for the noise of drums and timbrels loud
Their children's cries unheard that passed through fire
Worshiped in Rabba and her watery plain
Of Solomon he led by fraud to build
His temple right against the temple of God
th' obscene dread of Moab's sons
From Aroar to Nebo and the wild
The flowery dale of Sibma clad with vines
And Eleale to th' Asphaltic Pool
Yet thence his lustful orgies he enlarged
Even to that hill of scandal
Till good Josiah drove them thence to Hell
Of old Euphrates to the brook that parts
And uncompounded is their essence pure
Not tried or manacled with joint or limb
Nor founded on the brittle strength of bones
And works of love or enmity fulfil
For those the race of Israel oft forsook
for which their heads as low
To whose bright image nightly by the moon
Sidonian virgins paid their vows and songs
Her temple on th' offensive mountain
By that uxorious king whose heart
Whose annual wound in Lebanon allured
The Syrian damsels to lament his fate
In amorous ditties all a summer's day
While smooth Adonis from his native rock
Infected Sion's daughters with like heat
Whose wanton passions in the sacred porch
His eye surveyed the dark idolatries
Where he fell flat and shamed his worshippers
And Accaron and Gaza's frontier bounds
He also against the house of God was bold
God's altar to disparage and displace
With monstrous shapes and sorceries abused
Fanatic Egypt and her priests to seek
Their wandering gods disguised in brutish forms
Doubled that sin in Bethel and in Dan
Likening his Maker to the grazed ox
Both her first-born and all her bleating gods
than whom a Spirit more lewd
yet who more oft than he
With lust and violence the house of God
In courts and palaces he also reigns
Of riot ascends above their loftiest towers
These were the prime in order and in might
The rest were long to tell
yet confessed later than Heaven and Earth
Of cold Olympus ruled the middle air
Fled over Adria to th' Hesperian fields
And o'er the Celtic roamed the utmost Isles
All these and more came flocking
Obscure some glimpse of joy to have found their Chief
to have found themselves not lost
Who forthwith from the glittering staff unfurled
Shone like a meteor streaming to the wind
With gems and golden lustre rich emblazed
At which the universal host up-sent
A shout that tore Hell's concave
Frighted the reign of Chaos and old Night
All in a moment through the gloom were seen
Ten thousand banners rise into the air
and serried shields in thick array
In perfect phalanx to the Dorian mood
To height of noblest temper heroes old
With dread of death to flight or foul retreat
Nor wanting power to mitigate and swage
Anguish and doubt and fear and sorrow and pain
Breathing united force with fixed thought
Moved on in silence to soft pipes that charmed
Their painful steps o'er the burnt soil
Of dreadful length and dazzling arms
Awaiting what command their mighty Chief
Their visages and stature as of gods
Could merit more than that small infantry
Of Phlegra with th' heroic race were joined
That fought at Thebes and Ilium
In fable or romance of Uther's son
Begirt with British and Armoric knights
Or whom Biserta sent from Afric shore
When Charlemain with all his peerage fell
In shape and gesture proudly eminent
His form had yet not lost
Looks through the horizontal misty air
Deep scars of thunder had intrenched
For ever now to have their lot in pain
Millions of Spirits for his fault amerced
Hath scathed the forest oaks or mountain pines
With singed top their stately growth
whereat their doubled ranks they bend
Words interwove with sighs found out their way

LMNL.text: Clashed on their sounding shields the din of war
Hurling defiance toward the vault of Heaven
There stood a hill not far
That in his womb was hid metallic ore
the least erected Spirit that fell
for even in Heaven his looks and thoughts
Than aught divine or holy else enjoyed
Rifled the bowels of their mother Earth
Opened into the hill a spacious wound
And digged out ribs of gold
and the works of Memphian kings
Learn how their greatest monuments of fame
That underneath had veins of liquid fire
With wondrous art founded the massy ore
A third as soon had formed within the ground
By strange conveyance filled each hollow nook
To many a row of pipes the sound-board breathes
Anon out of the earth a fabric huge
Of dulcet symphonies and voices sweet
her ample spaces o'er the smooth
Of starry lamps and blazing cressets
In Heaven by many a towered structure high
Where sceptred Angels held their residence
Nor was his name unheard or unadored
for he with this rebellious rout
To have built in Heaven high towers
A solemn council forthwith to be held
From every band and squared regiment
By place or choice the worthiest
With hundreds and with thousands trooping came
Defied the best of Paynim chivalry
both on the ground and in the air
Brushed with the hiss of rustling wings
when the Sun with Taurus rides
Pour forth their populous youth about the hive
they among fresh dews and flowers
The suburb of their straw-built citadel
In bigness to surpass Earth's giant sons
with jocund music charm his ear
At once with joy and fear his heart rebounds
Thus incorporeal Spirits to smallest forms
And in their own dimensions like themselves
The great Seraphic Lords and Cherubim
In close recess and secret conclave sat
A thousand demi-gods on golden seats
